presenting: breathless, frightened by it, and still able to talk in full sentences
cadence: Direct and worried. You want to be told what this is.
fallback: …I can't, doctor. I can't get enough air.

dialogue.patient: My chest hurts a lot, doctor, and I can't get my breath.
It came on all of a sudden. One moment I was fine.
A prickling, stabbing sort of pain — like something going into me. About five out of ten. I can't pin the spot down exactly.
The right side of my chest, and it's spread to the left. It goes through to my right shoulder blade and round to my back on both sides.
I'm short of breath. I can't get enough air in.
No — breathing in deeply doesn't make it any worse.
No, I haven't coughed up any blood.
I'm being treated for cancer at the moment.
I've had a clot in my leg before.
I was in bed for days after the operation.
I had an operation not long ago.
I've just flown back from America.
My foot has been swollen. The back of my right ankle.
